conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee, one of the surgery team doctors. I understand you’re here because of increasing pain at your G-tube site. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been getting worse over the last few days. It’s a deep, constant ache right where the tube comes out. I was in the pain clinic yesterday, and they said it might be inflammation from the tube itself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That matches what we’re seeing. Your CT scan shows some inflammation in the muscle around the tube, but no abscess or infection. We’ve seen this before—it’s a reaction to the presence of the tube.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I already had the tube changed recently, and it didn’t help. Why is it still hurting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sometimes the tissue becomes sensitized, and even a new tube can cause irritation. We tried injecting a steroid through the tube earlier, but you didn’t get much relief, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, it only helped a little for a few hours. Is there anything else we can do?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: For now, we’re focusing on pain control. We’ve switched you from oxycodone to dilaudid by mouth, which seems to be working better. How’s the pain now, on a scale from 1 to 10?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s about a 5 now. That’s much better than earlier—thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep that going as needed. You’re still on continuous tube feeds at 40 cc/hr, and we tried giving a bolus earlier, but your blood sugar dropped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I felt shaky and weak. I’ve had that before—my hypoglycemia kicks in fast.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. So we’ve gone back to continuous feeds to keep your sugars stable. We’ll send you home on NutriHep at 50 cc/hour. You’ll need to keep checking your blood sugar regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can do that. But what about the tube? The pain clinic said it might need to be removed or replaced.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s something to discuss with your surgeon. Right now, removing it isn’t urgent since there’s no infection. But if the pain continues, we may need to consider it. For now, we’re managing the inflammation and pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You made it through the night well—vitals are stable, no fever, and your pain has been controlled. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. Will I still have the pain at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll have dilaudid to take as needed every 4 hours. If the pain isn’t improving within a day or gets worse, please call your surgeon or come back. Also, watch for fever, redness, or drainage at the site.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I’ll keep the feeds going continuously and check my sugars?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Continue all your regular medications too, unless told otherwise. You have a follow-up with your surgeon soon—we’ll go over next steps then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Just take it easy, stay hydrated, and don’t drive while on the pain meds. We’ll get your discharge papers ready shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave—we reviewed your discharge instructions. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, everything’s clear. I’ll follow up with my surgeon and keep an eye on my symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again for your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will bring your prescriptions and discharge paperwork now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready when she is.
